bio: Halfway between the neighbourhoods of Recoleta and Retiro, this business is run by three siblings of Dutch origin and surprises for its concept, with a corner café on the ground floor (Presencia Gran Café) and the elegant gastronomic restaurant on the upper floor, with a much more discreet adjoining entrance and lift. With its French-Mediterranean nouvelle cuisine character and lots of Argentine flair, the food is under the charge of chef Rodrigo Da Costa, who despite his youth has worked in prestigious European restaurants (such as the three-starred Mirazur), was a professor at the Argentine Institute of Gastronomy and formed part of the national team in the Bocuse d'Or competition. It focuses on à la carte dining, with intriguing dishes like the burrata served with white gazpacho, sun-dried tomato chutney, pickled fennel and buckwheat crisp, or the black hake served with cauliflower and miso purée, vanilla and vodka beurre blanc.
